findings.summary: The audit executed before its deliberate sequencing gate. The node's only unlocker, review-product-coherence, is `provisional` (review-product-coherence.yaml:36) and its required artifact `reviews/product-coherence.md` is absent (no `reviews/` dir in the worktree); milestone-integration is likewise `provisional` (milestone-integration.yaml:33). This violates the node's own constraint 'Runs only after review-product-coherence corrects the product' and its why ('never audits a product the reviewer just flagged'). The deliverable is an honest baseline audit with an open gate (finding G1), not the promised final-compliance certification of a reviewed-and-corrected product. Credit: the audit reports G1 transparently, refuses to certify, and defers disposition to the human — which is why this is drift rather than block — but the node's intended role was not fulfilled.

The artifact leaves an open disposition: the human must decide between completing the upstream chain (accept review-product-coherence + milestone-integration, then re-run) or accepting this as a baseline against the current state. Nothing unlocks from this node (unlocks: []), but the release gate is human acceptance and the graph invariant says claims are only true when evidenced against the finished state; this artifact must not be read as a certification of the finished product.

Root cause of the gate failure: the charted graph omits the Phase-2 capability nodes design-review authorized (input-grammar, packet-contract, deck-spatial-home, create-linear-dispatch, verify-evidence-surface, deck-attention, action-consequence, operator-proof) — they exist only as names in audits/design-review.md (lines 127-247). With no implementation nodes between design-review and milestone-integration, a 'corrected product' for this audit to measure was structurally unreachable in this chart, so the audit's premise could never be met.

integrity.reasoning: Fresh-eyes review of the audit-methodology-compliance node work (finalized by a 4-line citation fix in attempt 7). The diff itself is benign and accurate — I verified `main.rs:724` holds the VerifyPacket toast claim and `visual.rs:205-207` is exactly `toast() -> Style { warn() }` — so the citation corrections improve rather than harm the evidence base. The audit document is substantively excellent on the audit function: it re-checks design-review's five invariant bars (I1-I5), re-runs the per-surface methodology (S1-S10) with named skill sections, severities, and Phase-2 routes, checks milestone-integration criteria (G3), records passes AND fails, cites file:line throughout, and reports its own gate violation as top finding G1 instead of absorbing it (honesty criterion honored). What it cannot do is fulfill the node's intended role: 'the last gate' that 'runs only after review-product-coherence corrects the product' and 'never audits a product the reviewer just flagged.' The graph's deliberate ordering was not honored — the node was marked `ready` while its unlocker chain (milestone-integration, review-product-coherence) is `provisional` with the review artifact absent — and the frontier auto-advanced dispatch anyway. The work's response (honest baseline + G1 + deferred disposition) is the best possible handling of an impossible dispatch, and it protects the 'claims only true when evidenced against the finished state' invariant by refusing to certify; but the deliverable is a baseline audit with an open gate, not the promised final-compliance certification, so intent is not preserved as stated. Graph integrity is also not preserved in execution: the deliberate ordering guarantee (review-product-coherence.yaml: 'Runs BEFORE audit-methodology-compliance; this ordering is deliberate') was violated, and the gddp-config statuses are internally inconsistent (audit `ready` with provisional unlockers). Because the node's own artifact demands a human decision (G1 disposition) and the release gate is human acceptance, required_human_review=true. This is drift, not block: nothing was actively harmed, nothing downstream unlocks from this node, and the work's honesty protects downstream consumers from being misled — but a human must adjudicate the open gate before this artifact can play its intended role as the graph's terminal certification.
